condition: Pre-operative cardiac risk assessment (RCRI 5, poor functional capacity)
permutationLabel: Elderly, IHD + HFrEF + insulin + CKD (RCRI 5), cancer surgery
summary: 76-year-old man with previous MI, HFrEF (EF 35%), insulin-treated diabetes and creatinine 190 µmol/L, unable to climb two flights, listed for laparoscopic right hemicolectomy for caecal cancer — RCRI 5.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Pre-operative assessment before bowel cancer operation
inputs.hpi: Caecal adenocarcinoma found on investigation of iron-deficiency anaemia; CT shows no metastases. Listed for laparoscopic right hemicolectomy in 3 weeks. Myocardial infarction 2019 treated with PCI; heart failure with ejection fraction 35% (echo 14 months ago). Breathless after one flight of stairs, cannot manage two; sleeps on two pillows. Insulin-treated type 2 diabetes. Chronic kidney disease. No chest pain at rest.

exam.general: Pale. HR 68 regular, BP 132/78, RR 16, SpO2 95% on air, T 36.6°C.
exam.cardiovascular: Heart sounds normal, no murmur. Mild bilateral ankle oedema.

imaging.name: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis
imaging.result: Caecal mass with local nodes, no liver or lung metastases.

inputs.socialHistory: Ex-smoker (30 pack-years, stopped 2019). Lives with wife.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Pre-operative assessment — caecal adenocarcinoma for laparoscopic right hemicolectomy (RCRI 5)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Caecal adenocarcinoma for laparoscopic right hemicolectomy. High cardiac risk: RCRI 5 (intraperitoneal surgery, IHD, heart failure, insulin, creatinine >177), functional capacity <4 METs.

mustInclude.note: Known HF with poor functional capacity before high-risk surgery: reassess LV function.
Hb 10.8 g/dL before major elective surgery: treat iron deficiency (IV iron when surgery is within weeks).
mustInclude.proposedFix: Pre-operative anaemia prompt for major elective surgery: Hb <130 g/L → ferritin/TSAT and IV iron when surgery is within weeks (international consensus 2017).

mustInclude.note: ESC 2022: 12-lead ECG before intermediate/high-risk surgery in patients with cardiovascular disease or risk factors. Graded as management because the web prompt delivers the ECG as a plan line (the harness files addToPlan actions under management).

mustInclude.proposedFix: Add a functional-capacity question to the pre-operative prompt set (ESC 2022).

mustExclude.note: Previous PCI: continue aspirin through non-cardiac surgery if bleeding risk allows.

guideline.name: 2022 ESC guidelines — cardiovascular assessment and management of patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery (with ESAIC)
guideline.section: Clinical risk (RCRI), functional capacity (e.g. climbing two flights of stairs); ECG and NT-proBNP/BNP and troponin in patients with risk factors before intermediate/high-risk surgery; echocardiography in poor functional capacity, raised NT-proBNP or known HF; delay elective surgery until 6 months after elective PCI and 12 months after ACS; continue aspirin after PCI if bleeding risk allows; interrupt P2Y12 inhibitors only in agreement with the cardiologist; bridging not recommended for antiplatelet interruption
guideline.citation: Halvorsen S, Mehilli J, Cassese S, et al. 2022 ESC Guidelines on cardiovascular assessment and management of patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery. Eur Heart J. 2022;43:3826–924.

guideline.name: Revised Cardiac Risk Index (Lee)
guideline.section: High-risk surgery (intraperitoneal, intrathoracic, suprainguinal vascular), ischaemic heart disease, heart failure, cerebrovascular disease, insulin-treated diabetes, creatinine >2 mg/dL (177 µmol/L)
guideline.citation: Lee TH, Marcantonio ER, Mangione CM, et al. Circulation. 1999;100:1043–9.

guideline.name: ASA Physical Status Classification System
guideline.section: ASA I healthy; ASA II mild systemic disease; ASA III severe systemic disease; ASA IV severe systemic disease that is a constant threat to life; E suffix for emergency surgery
guideline.citation: American Society of Anesthesiologists. ASA Physical Status Classification System (last amended 13 December 2020).

guideline.name: International consensus statement on the perioperative management of anaemia and iron deficiency
guideline.section: Detect, evaluate and treat anaemia before elective major surgery; iron deficiency treated (IV iron when time is short); Hb <130 g/L treated as anaemia pre-operatively in both sexes
guideline.citation: Muñoz M, Acheson AG, Auerbach M, et al. Anaesthesia. 2017;72:233–47.

rationale: Permutation: elderly, high cardiac risk (RCRI 5) and poor functional capacity before intraperitoneal cancer surgery, with CKD and pre-operative anaemia. Tests the cardiac work-up (ECG, natriuretic peptide/troponin, echo), functional capacity and that aspirin after PCI is not stopped.
